description: Searched only snapshots/s02 for firmware-table-divisor variants of the seed's zero/overflow-denominator mechanism. Bounded negative result for the firmware-table branch itself: atom.c firmware interpreter guards src != 0 (lines 695/715); AMD smumgr do_div sites divide by per-ASIC driver constants (ref_clock via amdgpu_asic_get_xclk, vegam_smumgr.c:764, polaris10_smumgr.c:933/948); si.c:1734 divides by atombios reference_freq (fixed 10kHz-unit value, not attacker-influenced); smu_v11_0.c:1281 and arcturus_ppt.c:1222 guard tach_status; si_dpm.c:6722 is '#if 0' dead code. However the same snapshot contains one credible unpatched seed-mechanism variant, recorded as the finding: drivers/gpu/drm/amd/pm/swsmu/smu11/smu_v11_0.c lines 1215-1217, 'tach_period = 60 * crystal_clock_freq * 10000 / (8 * speed);' in smu_v11_0_set_fan_speed_rpm, where only the raw 'speed == 0' is validated (line 1206) while the u32 expression 8*speed wraps to 0 for speed > UINT_MAX/8 — sibling implementations (vega20_thermal.c:194, arcturus_ppt.c:1270, smu_v13_0.c:1229) carry the UINT_MAX/8 bound but this one does not; reachable via navi10_ppt.c:3589 and sienna_cichlid_ppt.c:3199 fan RPM store paths. Confidence medium (user-interface rather than firmware-table source; hwmon-layer clamping not re-verified). Limitations: non-AMD ACPI/SMBIOS/EDID/DT/EEPROM divisor parses not fully swept, display/dc do_div sites not all individually triaged.
